description: Secure Flight marks selected passengers with SSSS (or S) on the boarding pass, triggering enhanced screening - intensive search, enhanced pat-down, sometimes powering on every device. It can happen at the checkpoint, a separate area, or at the gate, and applies to flights to, from, within and overflying the US.
source_name: TSA Secure Flight / Secondary Security Screening Selection

description: There is no public statistic on SSSS designation rates for Iranian travellers. The documented profiling evidence is land-border, not airport.
energy_note: A pattern everyone experiences and nobody can measure.
notes: HONEST LIMIT: the disproportion is widely reported and NOT statistically established. ACLU/CAIR/NIAC FOIA records are the place to dig - layer-5 target.

description: In January 2020, lawmakers asked CBP whether officers had questioned US travellers at airports, and requested any directives on 'the screening of individuals of Iranian heritage' after Soleimani's killing - indicating the concern was not confined to Blaine.
Arrive hours early every flight, keep every device charged, expect to miss tight connections. For frequent flyers the cumulative cost is days per year.
time_note: Per flight; compounding across a year.
source_name: The Points Guy - the dreaded SSSS

description: DHS TRIP exists for redress, but a selectee is never told why they were selected, so there is nothing specific to rebut.

Senators recorded that people subjected to prolonged inspection - including US citizens and permanent residents - were asked about political views, allegiances, social media profiles, family relationships and military service.
energy_note: Your own citizenship does not end the interrogation.

aspect: SCENARIO - eleven SSSS in fourteen flights
description: Omid keeps a note in his phone. Across fourteen flights in two years his boarding pass was stamped SSSS eleven times. He now books the earliest flight of the day and arrives three and a half hours early, every time, and has stopped booking connections under two hours.
time_note: About 45 hours a year in extra airport time.
energy_note: A private statistic nobody will accept as evidence.
